facts.text: Deep Ellum earned the nickname "Dallas's Soho" when artists, musicians, and entrepreneurs revived abandoned warehouses in the mid‑1980s.
The neighborhood’s roots trace back to railroads that built Deep Elm, giving the area its name and early industrial character.
In 1991, artist Frank Campagna organized TunnelVisions, commissioning murals along the Good‑Latimer Expressway tunnel that still color the streets today.
Deep Ellum’s music scene attracted blues legends like Leadbelly and Blind Lemon Jefferson, who performed in local clubs during the 1920s recording boom.
The former Dallas Landmark building was converted into loft apartments in 1997, preserving its historic façade while adding modern living space.
The Deep Ellum Archive, partnered with the Dallas Public Library, curates the neighborhood’s rich history for researchers and the public.
